why: MY OWN READ, NOT BOB'S. Every figure comes from the vetted read tools run on 2026-09-20 as the read-only role; rows and meta are recorded whole and every mark binds to a field of them. The prose, the claims, the questions and the arrangement are the SESSION'S. NO MODEL TURN WAS SPENT. The lead read - each day against the SAME WEEKDAY of the baseline week - is the one the tool refused until this session fixed it (comparisons.previous_period.valid_time_buckets).
question: how are our stores?
answer:
The shops are **fine, and the week-on-week headline is one Monday.**

Six of seven days beat the same day a week earlier. The one that did not is a Monday, against a Monday that took nearly double what a Monday takes here - nothing here says why. What separates the shops is what a visit is worth: Fairview grew basket on fewer people, Greenhills the opposite.

Shall I set a watch on Greenhills' basket, so it only speaks if it keeps going?

blocks.question: Is the estate actually having a worse week?
blocks.claim: Six of the seven days beat the same day a week earlier
blocks.thought: Each day against the same weekday before it. Only the Monday is down, and it is down against a Monday that was unlike any other.

blocks.question: And by shop?
blocks.claim: Four up, and only one materially down
blocks.thought: OPUS carries the whole of the estate's shortfall; North Edsa and Greenhills give back a little.

blocks.question: Is any part of the range carrying it?
blocks.claim: Everything is a little softer and nothing is the story
blocks.thought: Toys and seasonal fall hardest in proportion; the big categories barely move.

blocks.question: Are they serving more people, or fewer?
blocks.claim: Mixed, and the movement is small either way
blocks.thought: Shangri-La and Greenhills busier; Fairview and North Edsa quieter.

blocks.question: And what is a visit worth?
blocks.claim: This is where the shops actually differ
blocks.thought: Fairview grew basket while serving fewer people - fewer, better visits.

children.say: So the week is not the story. One Monday is, and it is a Monday in the week we are measuring against rather than in this one.
Where the shops genuinely differ is not how many people came in. It is what each visit was worth.

children.heading: Visits, and what each one was worth

reading.claim: fine, and the week-on-week headline is one Monday
reading.caveat: The comparison is the closed week 7-13 Sep against 31 Aug-6 Sep, each day against the same weekday. What made 31 August take nearly twice a normal Monday is not something any read here settles.
reading.next: I would watch Greenhills' basket for one more week rather than act on it - shall I set that as a watch, so it only speaks if it keeps going?
